headline_marked: [[Google Play Store will force apps to stop hogging RAM]] by February 2027, improving Android performance
headline: Google Play Store will force apps to stop hogging RAM by February 2027, improving Android performance
summary: New requirements for app developers, effective February 2027, aim to curb excessive memory use across dynamic memory, bitmap, and code optimization, with non-compliant apps facing reduced visibility.
details: Google Play Store is introducing new requirements for app developers to curb excessive memory usage on Android devices. This initiative aims to improve overall user experience by preventing system-wide slowdowns caused by memory-hungry applications.

The move comes as the mobile industry faces significant hardware supply constraints, impacting device memory availability. Android is addressing this challenge to protect user experience from apps consuming too much RAM.

By February 2027, Android apps must meet "bad behavior thresholds" across dynamic memory usage, bitmap usage, and code optimization. These limits are designed to prevent unexpected on-device performance throttling and app terminations.

Apps that fail to comply with these new memory limits will not be banned from the Play Store. Instead, they will face "reduced app visibility and publishing capabilities," encouraging developers to optimize their applications.

Google plans to release more details later this year, with thresholds adapting over time to align with advancements in Android and new devices. This is part of broader efforts to enhance the Android ecosystem.

In a related announcement, Google also stated that Android apps will need to support Zero-Tap Sign-In by April 2027. This feature aims to simplify device switching by automatically signing users into their apps on new devices.

headline_marked: [[Stripe acquires Clerky]], expanding its startup ecosystem services
headline: Stripe acquires Clerky, expanding its startup ecosystem services
summary: Clerky is the most popular online legal service for top startups, accounting for 23% of Silicon Valley seed/pre-seed financings and over $140 billion in raised capital.
details: Clerky, a leading online legal service for startups, has announced its acquisition by Stripe. The move aims to further support the startup ecosystem by integrating Clerky's expertise in routine legal paperwork.
For over a decade, Clerky has helped startups and their attorneys streamline legal processes, preventing costly fixes later. Its services are used by hundreds of attorneys and paralegals.

Clerky startups represent 23% of all Silicon Valley seed/pre-seed financings and have collectively raised over $140 billion in venture capital. The company saw 6.5x faster startup formation growth in the past year.
Both companies share a mission to empower startups. Clerky will continue operating with its existing team and focus, now leveraging Stripe's resources to build new products and features.
